claims.title: Pushing into a non-full ArrayVec does not panic
claims.author: mira
claims.scope: T = u8; CAP = 8; x86_64; default features
claims.condition: The vector is valid and len(v) < 8. The new element is a u8.
claims.formula: ∀ v : ArrayVec<u8, 8>, x : u8. valid(v) ∧ len(v) < 8 ⇒ ¬panics(v.push(x))
claims.description: For the stated concrete type and capacity, push does not panic when at least one slot is available.
comments: Does this cover arbitrary capacities, or only CAP = 8? The original title reads as if this applies to all ArrayVec instantiations.
Only CAP = 8 and T = u8 in this harness. I have made the concrete instantiation explicit in revision 2. Generalizing over CAP is still open.
I reproduced the bounded result using the same assumptions. Could you also include the exact compiler version in the evidence?
The scope is clearer now. One remaining question: can we link the valid(v) predicate to the initialization used in the harness?

claims.title: try_push returns an error at capacity
claims.author: emil
claims.condition: A valid ArrayVec<u8, 8>; every possible length from 0 through 8.
claims.description: The full-capacity case is included. The result may be Err; success is not claimed.
comments: I included the full-capacity case and reproduced the reported result.

claims.title: Unchecked access within the initialized prefix
claims.author: soren
claims.scope: T = u8; CAP = 4; four example states
claims.condition: i < len(v), valid storage, and no conflicting mutable borrow.
claims.description: This is a proposed general statement. The attached example executions do not establish it for all inputs.

claims.title: The inline-to-heap transition preserves initialized elements
claims.author: nora
claims.condition: Valid initial state; allocator succeeds; no external aliasing.
claims.description: Example runs exercise the spill boundary. This is not a universal proof.
comments: Have you also exercised zero-sized element types? The current evidence only covers u8.
Not yet. The claim is scoped to u8; a separate claim would be needed for other element types.

claims.title: Slicing with ordered, in-bounds endpoints
claims.author: mira
claims.condition: 0 ≤ start ≤ end ≤ len(b); a valid Bytes value.
claims.formula: ∀ b, s, e. valid(b) ∧ len(b) ≤ 16 ∧ 0 ≤ s ≤ e ≤ len(b) ⇒ ¬panics(b.slice(s..e))
claims.description: The empty range and the endpoint at len(b) are included.
comments: Reproduced with empty buffers and empty ranges included.
Useful to make Range<usize> explicit: this does not cover every RangeBounds implementation.

claims.title: Byte search on bounded slices
claims.author: emil
claims.scope: Scalar implementation; slices up to 32 bytes
claims.condition: Valid byte slice with length ≤ 32; SIMD disabled.
claims.description: The scalar implementation is the only implementation in scope.
comments: Please record how the scalar implementation was selected in this run.

claims.title: Checked indexing over arbitrary valid slices
claims.author: soren
claims.scope: Abstract valid slices; pure element access
claims.condition: A valid slice; i is any usize.
comments: The None branch makes the boundary condition explicit.

claims.title: Unconditional split_at claim
claims.author: mira
claims.condition: The original claim imposed no restriction on mid.
claims.description: Withdrawn after a counterexample. A revised claim needs mid ≤ len(s).
comments: An empty slice with mid = 1 panics. The precondition needs to bound mid by the slice length.
Agreed. I have withdrawn this claim rather than silently changing its statement.

claims.title: Overflow is returned as a parse error
claims.author: nora
claims.condition: Input is ASCII and contains at most ten bytes.
claims.description: Overflow and invalid digits are represented as errors by this API.

claims.title: No panic for u16 vectors with capacity 4
claims.author: emil
claims.condition: Valid vector with length less than 4.
claims.formula: ∀ v : ArrayVec<u16, 4>, x : u16. valid(v) ∧ len(v) < 4 ⇒ ¬panics(v.push(x))
claims.description: A separate bounded claim with different element type and capacity.

claims.title: Initialized writes into spare capacity
claims.author: soren
claims.condition: The vector is valid and len(v) < 8. The new element is a u8.
claims.description: A general proposition supported only by sample executions, not a universal proof.

claims.title: Push preserves the storage invariant for capacity 4
claims.author: nora
claims.condition: Valid vector and len(v) < 4; standard allocator model.
